headline: The Case for Vibe Coding Your Next Presentation
lede: For decades, presentations have been the domain of drag-and-drop software — tools optimized for ease at the cost of expressive range. A GitHub repository called frontend-slides proposes a different arrangement: describe what you want to an AI, receive a self-contained HTML file, and never open a traditional slide editor again. The project's creator marked the milestone of 1,000 GitHub stars with the casual observation that she now vibe codes pretty much all her presentations in HTML.
body:
The skill, created by Zara Zhang (posting as @zarazhangrui), a Bay Area technologist and self-described humanist who calls herself “not a coder,” works through a deliberate onboarding sequence. Claude first interviews the user about the presentation's purpose and aesthetic sensibility. It then generates three distinct HTML preview files — each drawn from one of twelve curated visual presets with names like Electric Studio, Swiss Modern, or Terminal Green — so the user selects by seeing rather than by describing. The output is a single **zero-dependency HTML file** with all CSS and JavaScript inlined: no frameworks, no build steps, no package manager required. One design constraint, stated in the skill's own instruction file as “non-negotiable,” governs every slide: it must fit within a single viewport height, forbidding the cognitive dissonance of a slide that scrolls.

frontend-slides is a **Claude Code skill** — a structured markdown instruction file, stored locally and invoked as the slash command `/frontend-slides`, that teaches Claude a repeatable multi-phase workflow complete with quality constraints and tool-call instructions. The *skill system*, developed by Anthropic, is analogous to a macro or template, except the “code” is prose. An update in early 2026 reduced the skill's main instruction file from 1,625 lines to 183 — an 89% *context-window* reduction achieved by applying *progressive disclosure*: loading supporting files on demand rather than front-loading everything into the prompt. The optimization borrows a standard software-design discipline and applies it to the architecture of natural language.

The repo exemplifies *vibe coding*, a phrase coined by former OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy in February 2025 for an approach in which the human describes desired outcomes, evaluates what the AI returns, and iterates — without writing code directly. Presentations are arguably the practice's first truly universal use case: not a side-project app or an internal tool, but something nearly every knowledge worker produces. Zhang says she now “vibe codes pretty much all my presentations on html.” The skill was itself built this way: she iterated with Claude dozens of times until the output cleared her quality bar, then instructed Claude to encode that accumulated workflow into a reusable skill. The tool is recursively self-demonstrating.

A developer ecosystem for code-based slides already exists — Reveal.js (roughly 67,000 GitHub stars), *Slidev* (Vue-based, around 30,000 stars), and *Marp* (over two million Visual Studio Code installs). These tools share an honest trade-off: version control and composability in exchange for drag-and-drop authoring, but they still require the presenter to write the code. frontend-slides occupies a distinct niche: it inherits the browser-native, zero-dependency philosophy of Reveal.js while eliminating the authoring barrier entirely. The correct frame is not “AI version of Microsoft (MSFT) PowerPoint” but “AI-mediated access to the web-native presentation paradigm.”

The 1,000-star milestone prompted the announcement tweet. The repo has since grown substantially — largely without mainstream press coverage, carried instead by word of mouth within the Claude Code community and AI-builder circles on X. Third-party *skill-marketplace* aggregators have catalogued it as a productivity shortcut for non-designers in operations. A community fork has extended the original with drag-resize editing and slide reordering. The broader implication is that the Claude Code skill ecosystem is becoming a new distribution layer for AI-native workflows, bypassing traditional technology media entirely.

concepts.definition: A term coined by Andrej Karpathy in 2025 for a programming approach in which the human describes desired outcomes to an AI, evaluates its output, and iterates — without writing code directly. The word captures a shift in agency: the human becomes the taste-maker and editor, the AI the executor. Collins English Dictionary named it Word of the Year for 2025.

A markdown instruction file stored in a local directory that teaches Claude Code a repeatable workflow, invoked via a slash command. Skills encode multi-step processes — including quality constraints, phased execution, and tool calls — in structured natural language rather than code. They can be shared, installed, and distributed through community marketplaces.

A web document that contains all of its CSS styling and JavaScript behavior inlined within a single file, requiring no external libraries, build tools, or server infrastructure. Such files can be shared as a single attachment and opened in any browser without setup.

A design pattern in which a system reveals information incrementally, loading details only when needed rather than all at once. Applied here to prompt engineering, it means loading supporting instruction files on demand to preserve limited context-window space — the same principle that governs good UI design, applied to natural language.

The maximum amount of text a language model can process in a single interaction, measured in tokens. Instructions, conversation history, and generated output all count against this limit, making compact, well-structured prompts a meaningful practical optimization.

An emerging ecosystem of third-party Claude Code skills distributed through community aggregator sites and installed via Claude Code's plugin system. It functions as an informal app store for AI workflows, where contributors publish instruction files that others can download and invoke as slash commands.

repos.summary: A Claude Code skill that generates zero-dependency HTML presentations from a conversational brief. Claude interviews the user about aesthetics, presents three visual-direction previews drawn from twelve curated style presets, and outputs a single self-contained HTML file with all CSS and JavaScript inlined. The project crossed 1,000 GitHub stars organically and has since become one of the most-distributed skills in the Claude Code community.
